n: Peter and John go up to the temple at three in the afternoon, a set time of prayer. The apostles keep worshipping at the temple as faithful Jews.

f.g: About 3 p.m., the time of the evening sacrifice and prayer.

n: A man unable to walk from birth is carried every day to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he begs from worshippers.

f.g: Over forty years old (Acts 4:22), with no hope of a cure.
Probably the ornate bronze Nicanor Gate on the east side of the temple courts.
alms = gifts of money to the poor.

n: Seeing Peter and John about to enter, he asks them for money.
Peter looks intently at him, together with John, and says, “Look at us.” They give him their full attention.

f.g: Gazing intently — a recurring phrase in Luke’s writings.

n: The man looks up, expecting a coin.
Peter has no money, but offers what he does have — the power of Christ’s name: “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk.”

f.w: Silver and gold have I none
In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth

n: Peter takes his right hand and lifts him up, and at once his feet and ankles grow strong.

f.w: he took him by the right hand

n: He leaps to his feet, walks, and goes into the temple with them — walking, jumping, and praising God. A man once kept outside now enters God’s house.

f.g: Isaiah foretold that in the messianic age “the lame man [shall] leap as an hart.”

n: Everyone sees him walking and praising God.
They recognize him as the beggar from the Beautiful Gate and are filled with wonder at what happened.
Clinging to Peter and John, the healed man draws a crowd that comes running to Solomon’s Porch, astonished.

f.w: the porch that is called Solomon's
f.g: A covered colonnade along the east side of the temple’s outer court.

n: Peter seizes the moment: why are they amazed, and why stare at the apostles as if their own power or holiness did this?

f.w: as though by our own power or holiness

n: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has glorified his servant Jesus — the one they handed over and rejected before Pilate, even when Pilate wanted to release him.

f.w: The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob

f.g: Greek pais, “servant” or “child” — likely echoing Isaiah’s Servant of the Lord (Isaiah 52:13).

f.w: when he was determined to let him go

n: They rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be released instead.

f.w: the Holy One and the Just

n: They killed the very Author of life — a stunning paradox — but God raised him from the dead, and the apostles are witnesses.

f.g: Greek archēgos — originator, pioneer, author. Hebrews 12:2 uses the same word.

n: It is Jesus’s name, through faith in that name, that has made this man completely whole in front of them all.
Peter softens: he knows they and their leaders acted in ignorance.
God used even their actions to fulfill what all the prophets foretold: that the Messiah would suffer.
So repent and turn back to God so their sins may be wiped away, and times of refreshing may come from the Lord’s presence.

f.g: converted = turned around, turned back to God.
A period of spiritual renewal and rest given by God.

n: And God will send the Messiah appointed for them — Jesus — at his return.

Heaven must hold Jesus until the time of the restoration of all things foretold by the prophets. Latter-day Saints see this as pointing to the latter-day Restoration of the gospel before the Second Coming.

f.w: the times of restitution of all things

n: Moses foretold that God would raise up a prophet like him, whom the people must heed. Jesus himself identified himself as that prophet, and Moroni quoted these words to Joseph Smith.

f.w: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you

n: Anyone who refuses to listen to that prophet will be cut off from God’s people.

f.w: shall be destroyed from among the people

n: Every prophet from Samuel onward also foretold these days.

f.g: Samuel anointed David, from whose line the Messiah would come.

n: They are heirs of the prophets and of God’s covenant with Abraham: through his seed all families of the earth will be blessed.

f.w: in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed

n: God sent his risen Servant to them first, to bless them by turning each of them from their wickedness. The gospel went to Israel first, then to the Gentiles.

f.w: in turning away every one of you from his iniquities
